slides.answer: My friend — the name after Dear
slides.feedback: Emails keep Dear. The name after Dear is the reader.
slides.hint: Look after the word Dear. A name is there.
slides.notes: 0:00-2:00. Most pupils pick B (the 08-09 rule) — welcome it, then correct: in EMAILS the reader is the named friend, not the marker. Kill 'no Dear, no From' explicitly: emails KEEP Dear. Latecomers: repeat the one-liner 'We write to a friend today, not the marker.'
options: My friend — the name after Dear
slides.prompt: New system starts today. In EMAILS, who do you write to?

visual.alt: Magnifying glass, signalling detective work: find the clues

slides.hint: Find the word Dear. Read the name.
slides.notes: 2:00-4:00. Teacher circles the friend name after Dear (say it, point, pupils point). Say: 'The name after Dear is the reader. Every email starts here.' Deflect full-reading questions: 'Today we only find the reader. We write in Session 2.' The bracketed boxes are named only, not filled.
slides.prompt: We use one email every time. Point. Where is the reader?
slides.text: Dear [READER], How are you? I hope you are well. I am writing to you today. This message is important to me. Here is my message. [MAIN ANSWER]. First, [ANSWER 1]. Next, [ANSWER 2]. Also, [ANSWER 3]. Finally, [ANSWER 4]. That is all from me. Thank you for reading my message. I hope you understand it. Please write back soon. Best wishes, [MY NAME]

slides.hint: Circle the English word, not the Malay.
items: WHAT 📦 means apa — thing or action.
slides.notes: 4:00-10:00, ~1.5 min per clue. Exact script aloud: 'Circle WHAT. WHAT means apa.' / 'Circle WHERE. WHERE means di mana.' (parallel for WHEN/WHO). Elicit Malay first, then fix. Board drills (circle the English clue): What sport do you like? / Where do you play it? / When do you play it? / Who plays with you? One-liner pre-empt: 'WHICH is also apa — it means choose one.'
slides.prompt: Circle the clue. Say the Malay meaning.

slides.hint: How + feel asks for a feeling.
items: HOW ⚙️ means bagaimana, cara — action or way.
slides.notes: 10:00-14:00. Teach explicitly: 'feel after How = FEEL clue, the answer is a feeling.' Redirect answerers: 'Good answer. Now circle the clue word.' Fast round after reveal (oral, no new text): teacher says Malay, class says English — apa→WHAT, di mana→WHERE, bila→WHEN, siapa→WHO, mengapa→WHY, bagaimana→HOW, perasaan→FEEL.
slides.prompt: Circle the clue. Say the Malay meaning.

slides.hint: AND adds one box. TWO means two boxes.
items: TELL or INCLUDE means you must do it.
slides.notes: 14:00-18:00. Exact lines: 'I see AND. I need one more answer.' / 'I see TWO. I need two answers.' Board examples (circle the danger word): I like apples and oranges. / You have two free hours. / Tell me about your day. / Include your phone number. Distinguish once: TELL the danger word = an order inside the question; the TELL card = which email to write. Same word, two jobs.
slides.prompt: Danger! These words change your answers.

slides.answer: WHERE and WHO. Two questions, two boxes.
slides.feedback: Two questions need two answers. Hold up two fingers.
slides.hint: Two question words. No AND, no TWO.
slides.notes: 18:00-19:00. Pupils circle on the worksheet, then hold up fingers for the box count. Fast whole-class check.
slides.prompt: Circle every clue. Write the number of answers. Where do you play football? Who plays with you?

slides.answer: WHICH, WHY and AND. Two answers, not one.
slides.feedback: WHICH means choose one. AND joins two questions — two answers, not one.
slides.hint: WHICH is also apa. Find AND.
slides.notes: 19:00-20:00. Common miss: AND skipped, answer '1' — replay 'I see AND. I need one more answer.' WHICH belongs to the WHAT family (choose one).
slides.prompt: Circle every clue. Write the number of answers. Which drink do you like and why do you like it?

slides.answer: TWO and TELL. Two answers. You must do it.
slides.feedback: TWO means two answers. TELL only says you must answer.
slides.notes: 20:00-21:00. 'favourite' is not one of the seven circle clues — it is a TELL-card word for later (Beat 7); today circle TWO and TELL. TELL here is an order, not yet the green card.
slides.prompt: Circle every clue. Write the number of answers. You have two favourite games. Tell me about them.

slides.hint: Find SHOULD. Find tell, did, went or favourite. Find invite. Find sorry.
items: HELP is blue — should, suggest, recommend, advice.
TELL is green — tell, did, went, favourite, experience.
slides.notes: 22:00-26:00, 1 min per prompt. Four oral prompts (teacher reads, pupils hold up colour or say card): 1. Which sport should I choose? (HELP, blue — SHOULD) 2. Tell me about your favourite game. (TELL, green — tell and favourite; correct the WHAT-misfire: 'WHAT is the clue, but tell sets the job.') 3. I invite you to my party. (COME, orange — invite is stronger than tell) 4. I am sorry I broke your pen. (SORRY, red). Exact line: 'I see SHOULD. Choose the blue HELP card.' Keep colours visible; pointing is fine if no cards in hand. did/went are also TELL triggers (card row, toolkit, worksheet item 7).
slides.prompt: Which card? Hold up the colour.

slides.notes: 26:00-27:00. Read once straight through if needed, then point — do not teach from it. Keep this slide open (navigate back to it) during the guided model and the exit. No hints or reveals on a reference.
slides.prompt: Keep this open. Point to the row you need.
slides.text: Reader: the name after Dear — your friend. Clues: WHAT (apa, thing) · WHERE (di mana, place) · WHEN (bila, day or time) · WHO (siapa, person) · WHY (mengapa, sebab, reason) · HOW (bagaimana, cara, action or way) · FEEL (perasaan, feeling). Danger: AND (one more) · TWO (two) · TELL/INCLUDE (must do it). Cards: HELP blue (should, suggest, recommend, advice) · TELL green (tell, did, went, favourite, experience) · COME orange (invite) · SORRY red (apologise, sorry).

slides.answer: READER: friend. CARD: HELP. WHICH: badminton.
slides.feedback: SHOULD means advice, so HELP. WHICH means choose one.
slides.hint: Dear friend. I see SHOULD. Which colour card?
slides.notes: 27:00-28:00. Routine part 1 (pupils repeat and do): 'Circle WHAT — here WHICH, also apa. I see SHOULD. Choose the blue HELP card.'
slides.prompt: Reader, card, first clue. Which sport should I choose?

slides.answer: WHERE: school court. WHO: my friend.
slides.feedback: Two more questions, two more boxes.
slides.hint: WHERE asks the place. WHO asks the person.
slides.notes: 28:00-29:00. Routine part 2: 'Circle WHERE. Circle WHO. Three questions — three boxes.' Stop sentence-writing: 'Boxes today. Sentences in Session 2.'
slides.prompt: Same question. Finish the boxes. Where can I play it? Who can play with me?

slides.alt: Clipboard with a tick, signalling the independent exit check
slides.notes: 29:00-30:00. Independent evidence: pupils complete READER + CARD + CIRCLES + BOXES on worksheet Part 4 alone (slates/paper if sheets already used). Dictate the frame: READER / CARD (circle HELP·TELL·COME·SORRY) / CIRCLES / BOXES. Collect before revealing the key. Marking offline per the key.
slides.prompt: Alone. Show me: reader, card, circles, boxes. Which cartoon should I watch? Where can I watch it? Who watches with me?

slides.answer: READER: friend. CARD: HELP. CIRCLES: WHICH, WHERE, WHO. BOXES: 3.
slides.feedback: SHOULD gives HELP. Three questions, three boxes.
slides.hint: SHOULD points to HELP. Count the questions.
slides.notes: Reveal only after every sheet is collected. Pass = reader (friend) + HELP + at least 3 circles (WHICH/WHERE/WHO) + boxes 3. Fail patterns → Session 2 re-teach: wrong card (SHOULD→HELP), count under 3 (every question needs its box), reader = marker (Dear rule). Record aggregate only.
slides.prompt: Exit key. Mark after you collect every sheet.
